text: Three cups of popcorn: just twenty-four grams.
So how does a kernel get so big?
Inside, a drop of water turns to steam, bursts the hull, and puffs the starch into a light foam.
So three cups, air-popped: about ninety calories.
Popped in oil, one sixty-five; with a tablespoon of butter, two sixty-five; a tablespoon of sugar, over three hundred.
Same bowl, more than triple: count the grams and the toppings, not the size.
